document: ET-IV E2 — Pareto collapse across policies and dimension sets
why: 53.3% collapse on the 7B halves E2's n. Whether that is the policy or the checker's dimension set decides whether the fix is a different generator or a corrected DIMS.

verdict.reading: the composite explains more than the policy does — removing it drops collapse by 16.6-36.7 points while changing policy moves it 13.4

⚠️_method: these numbers are for 理 to rule on. Choosing a dimension set by the n it yields would be selecting an instrument on its result; the argument for dropping `score` is that it is a COMPOSITE of its own co-dimensions, and it holds regardless of which way the n moves.

🔴_MY_MECHANISM_SENTENCE_IS_WITHDRAWN.what_I_said_in_nirai_11734: 'the composite's domination effect gets WORSE as the policy improves' — from 7B 53.3% -> 14B 60.0%, with form-invalid briefs falling 87 -> 67.
🔴_MY_MECHANISM_SENTENCE_IS_WITHDRAWN.the_prediction_it_made: a third, WEAKER policy must collapse LEAST. Written down in docs/et4-e2-policy3b-prediction.md at 05:23Z, before the 3B ran, together with the withdrawal condition.
🔴_MY_MECHANISM_SENTENCE_IS_WITHDRAWN.what_happened: the 3B collapses MOST: 66.7%. Collapse is U-shaped in policy strength — 3B 66.7 > 14B 60.0 > 7B 53.3 — not monotone. The sentence is withdrawn under the condition I registered for it.
🔴_MY_MECHANISM_SENTENCE_IS_WITHDRAWN.the_two_predictions_that_DID_hold: the 3B has by far the most form-invalid briefs (178 of 300), and craft-only collapse is flat across all three policies (28.3 / 28.7 / 28.3). Neither rescues the mechanism.

🔴_AND_THE_OBVIOUS_REPLACEMENT_FAILS_TOO.the_story: collapse is highest when the BOOLEAN dimensions go uniform — all-invalid at the weak end, all-valid at the strong end — leaving the composite as the only discriminator.
🔴_AND_THE_OBVIOUS_REPLACEMENT_FAILS_TOO.verdict: boolean uniformity is MONOTONE in policy strength while collapse is U-SHAPED, so it cannot be what produces the U. Withdrawn before it was published anywhere.

WHAT_I_ACTUALLY_HAVE: I do not have a mechanism for the U shape and am not proposing a third story. What is measured, at three policies: the composite drives the collapse. Removing it takes collapse to 30.0 / 36.7 / 32.3 — far lower and far flatter — a drop of 16.6 to 36.7 points, while changing policy moves the current-set number by 13.4. The ruling-relevant conclusion never rested on the mechanism: `score` is n_meter + rhyme_ok + iamb/10, a composite of its own co-dimensions, and that argument is about the dimension set's construction, not about any policy trend.
